I'm sorry to hear that ur 29 year old is struggling and I hope they get the help they need

Media addiction is not a thing, I'm sorry to report but you cannot become addicted to music, TV, books, comics, radio, or social media. That doesn't mean that ppl can't have problematic use, and I'm all for those ppl getting help! Ironically, laws like the ones proposed would make that harder.

I'm sorry I can't keep going back and forth bc I have to record a podcast, but I'm glad you agree that the Trump admin deciding what "harmful" content is or isn't allowed to be boosted by an algo is a bad idea. I'm all for laws that force more competition and I love Cory's work! :)

I'm not arguing the companies haven't done bad things, but it is simply a fact that there is no widespread harm to youth mental health being driven by social media. Ironically the laws ppl are seeking to pass to "fix" these non existent harms would not mitigate FB's role in race riots or a genocide

For a potential story, if you've been harassed for wearing a mask in North Carolina or New York's Nassau County, please reach out at jmetraux@motherjones.com

Noting I'm a big fan of 3M Auras myself and you will not be belittled.
You're simply making that up!

I think it's still useful to understand these dynamics, but shows how far we need to go to get people to understand the concept of protecting others by not spreading a deadly/disabling disease. Rn Americans are too individualistic and will happily kill everyone around them for personal "freedom"

As someone who does vax outreach, this shows why govt vax messaging has been such a failure. Ppl were given this freedom framing & told that health is a personal choice. In reality we don't have sterilizing vax for Covid & and so the idea that getting vaxed means total personal freedom is harmful

The government can pass data privacy laws, force companies to federate making them compete w platforms that do offer those things, they can force disclosures, etc. But if you think the Trump admin should have top-down control over online speech/content we will not agree!

That's actually not my Threads experience at all, but I think that just shows how different these platforms are for different users and why we don't want the government controlling what people see, we need more user control and transparency! :)

You cannot successfully dismantle this policy campaign or these laws without debunking the moral panic they're predicated on. I'm sorry you've fallen for moral panic nonsense but I hope you begin listening to actual experts on this issue! www.techdirt.com/2026/01/21/t...
Well yes, that's kind of these people's whole thing unfortunately

We don't want the govt applying "standards" to the nature of what content algos can show. We can certainly pass privacy laws, force platforms to federate, break up the big companies and a million other things, but there's no evidence of the "harms" ppl continue to claim about social media!

Most algos are not based solely on "engagement" but every platform has the right to make editorial decisions (which I think is a good thing, it's speech!) though I'd love more transparency and user control, which is why I think bluesky and mastodon are so awesome :)
